simplicity.feedback: Excellent simplicity - each lesson has ONE clear goal, exactly 3 decision points, and substitute-friendly format. Very accessible for Grade 1 French Immersion.
strengths: Crystal clear single goal per lesson
Substitute teacher could use with 30 minutes notice
improvements: Could include more specific pronunciation guides for substitute teachers

progression.feedback: Strong progression from basic author concept to complete book creation. Vocabulary spirals well across lessons.
strengths: Clear progression: concept → ideas → drawing → words → complete story
Vocabulary builds logically (auteur → idée → dessiner → partager)
14 core lessons cover all expectations systematically
6 extensions provide meaningful practice without new content
improvements: Could reinforce some early vocabulary more frequently in later lessons

authenticity.feedback: Very authentic approach that supports teacher thinking and acknowledges classroom realities.
strengths: Supports teacher decision-making rather than scripting
Acknowledges unpredictability (shy students, quick finishers, etc.)
improvements: Could include more specific strategies for diverse learners
More explicit connection to French curriculum expectations

strengths: Perfect balance of structure and flexibility
Strong focus on creativity over perfection
Excellent scaffolding from teacher support to independence
recommendations: Add more specific French pronunciation guides
Include assessment rubric for portfolio evaluation
Provide more detailed vocabulary spiral tracking
Add connection to specific curriculum outcomes
